title: The Repo Rate in 60 Seconds

segments.say: One number, set in Mumbai, can change your home loan instalment and the interest on your fixed deposit. It's called the repo rate.

anim.title: What it is
items: It gives government bonds as security

segments.say: When a bank is short of cash, it can borrow from the Reserve Bank for a short time, giving government bonds as security. The interest it pays is the repo rate.

anim.title: Why 'repo'?
items: The bank sells bonds to the RBI

segments.say: Repo is short for repurchase. The bank sells bonds to the RBI and agrees to buy them back, a loan in disguise.
Raise the repo rate and loans get costlier, slowing spending and inflation. Cut it, and loans get cheaper, giving growth a push.
The repo rate sits in a corridor. Above it, the marginal standing facility, the ceiling. Below it, the standing deposit facility, where banks park spare cash.
The Monetary Policy Committee sets it, meeting about every two months. If the vote is tied, the Governor decides.
For GS Three and Prelims: repo is the rate at which the RBI lends to banks, the main lever of monetary policy.

sources: RBI, 'Monetary Policy' and FAQ on the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (rbi.org.in): repo rate as the policy rate; collateralised by government securities; Marginal Standing Facility as the upper bound; Standing Deposit Facility as the floor of the corridor since April 2022
RBI Act, 1934, section 45ZI: MPC decisions by majority; Governor has a casting vote in a tie; at least four meetings a year (in practice six)
NCERT Class 12 Macroeconomics, ch. 3: tools of monetary policy

quiz.q: The repo rate is the rate at which…
options: The RBI lends to banks against securities
quiz.why: Banks borrow from the RBI, giving bonds as security.

quiz.q: Which is the floor of the RBI's rate corridor today?
quiz.why: The SDF replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the floor in April 2022.

quiz.q: If the MPC vote is tied, who decides?
quiz.why: The Governor has a casting vote.

reviewNote: Facts were read against RBI's monetary policy pages and the RBI Act. The corridor bars are relative positions, not rates. Moving facts: the actual repo rate is deliberately not stated; it changes.
